title: Pneumonia, lung abscess, empyema and respiratory arrest in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the main lung condition (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026
Reason for Admission: aspiration pneumonia

Hospital Course:
Pt is a 56 y/o female admitted with aspiration pneumonia after choking on food at home. Pt presented with productive cough and fever. Initial labs and CXR confirmed diagnosis. Pt was started on IV antibiotics and monitored for clinical improvement. Pt remained stable on room air. Swallow evaluation was performed by SLP to assess risk of further aspiration. Pt tolerated oral intake and showed significant improvement in respiratory status. Discontinued IV meds and transitioned to PO.

Discharge Diagnoses:
- aspiration pneumonia

Discharge Medications:
- Amoxicillin 500mg BID x 7 days
- Guaifenesin 600mg PRN as needed

Follow-up:
F/u with primary care physician in 1 week. F/u with SLP as scheduled for continued swallow management.

Electronically signed,
D. Kowalski, MD
05/15/2026
explanations: Aspiration pneumonia: pneumonitis due to inhalation of food and vomit, J69.0 (HCC 282).
refs: ICD-10-CM Tabular: J15-J18, J69, J85-J86, R09

distractors.why: Aspiration pneumonia has its own code (HCC 282).
